'''The [[1984 in association football|1984]]–[[1985 in association football|85]] season''' was the 86th completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables and results ==

The tables and results below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1984-85.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website,<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1984-85.html |title=England 1984–85 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100127135010/http://www.rsssf.com/engpaul/FLA/1984-85.html| archive-date= 27 January 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> with home and away statistics separated.

During the first five seasons of the league, that is, until the season 1893–94, re-election process concerned the clubs which finished in the bottom four of the league. From the 1894–95 season and until the 1920–21 season the re-election process was required of the clubs which finished in the bottom three of the league. From the 1922–23 season on it was required of the bottom two teams of both Third Division North and Third Division South. Since the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] was established in the [[1958–59 Football League|1958–59 season]], the re-election process has concerned the bottom four clubs in that division.<ref>Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane's, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>

[[Howard Kendall]]'s [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] side beat neighbours [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to the league championship by thirteen points with five games to spare, while [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] followed closely behind. Kendall's team also collected the [[Cup Winners' Cup]]. [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] completed the top five, but long-serving manager [[Lawrie McMenemy]] then delivered a major surprise by resigning as manager to take over at relegated [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].

The season marked the return of [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] to the First Division after 14 years away, [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] after six years away, and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] after five years. All three sides secured First Division survival comfortably. 

[[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] finished bottom of the First Division with just three league wins all season and just 17 points – a record low under the 3 points for a win system in any division, which would stand for twenty-one years. [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] and Sunderland – the two League Cup finalists – occupied the two other relegation places.

Liverpool manager [[Joe Fagan]] retired after the season and striker [[Kenny Dalglish]] was appointed player-manager.

The First Division's leading scorers this season were [[Gary Lineker]] at [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and [[Kerry Dixon]] at Chelsea, with both players scoring 24 league goals.

==Second Division==
{{Infobox football league season
| competition        = [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]]
| season             = 1984–85
| winners            = [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]
| promoted           = [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]<br>[[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]]<br>[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]
| relegated          = [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]]<br>[[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]<br>[[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]
| league topscorer   = [[John Aldridge]]<br>(30 goals)<ref name="topscorers"/>

[[Jim Smith (footballer, born 1940)|Jim Smith]]'s [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] side won a successive promotion as Second Division champions and reached the First Division after just 23 years as Football League members. Following them into the big time were [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].

Slipping out of the league's second tier were [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], joined by [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] and [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] – both relegated for the second season in succession. Veteran manager [[Tommy Docherty]] had tried his hand at reversing financially troubled Wolves' rapid decline at Molineux, but without success.

==[[Football League Third Division|Third Division]]==

[[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]]'s Third Division championship was overshadowed on the final day of the season, when [[Bradford City stadium fire|a fire]] at their [[Valley Parade]] ground killed 56 spectators – including two followers of their opponents [[Lincoln City F.C.|Lincoln City]].

The other two promotion places in the Third Division were occupied by [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] and [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].

[[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]], [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Orient]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] went down from the Third Division. Burnley and Preston were founder members of the Football League, and 25 years prior, Burnley had been league champions.

[[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], who had finished sixth in the First Division just three years earlier, continued to decline as a result of their financial problems, as they narrowly avoided a third successive relegation.

==[[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]]==
{{Infobox football league season
 | competition        = [[Football League]][[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]]

[[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]], [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]], [[Darlington F.C.|Darlington]] and [[Bury F.C.|Bury]] were promoted to the Third Division after occupying the Fourth Division's top four places.

The bottom four clubs, [[Halifax Town A.F.C.|Halifax Town]], [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]], [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]], who had spent a season in the First Division 20 years earlier, and [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]], all retained their league status after a successful re-election campaign at the expense of [[Bath City F.C.|Bath City]], who were placed 4th in the [[Alliance Premier League]] and were the highest placed team there that would have met the Football League's requirements.

==Election/re-election to the Football League==

This year the top three teams in the [[1984–85 Alliance Premier League]], [[Wealdstone F.C.|Wealdstone]], [[Nuneaton Town F.C.|Nuneaton Borough]] and [[Dartford F.C.|Dartford]], could not apply for election because they did not meet [[Football League]] requirements, so fourth-placed [[Bath City F.C.|Bath City]] won the right to apply for election to the Football League to replace one of the four bottom sides in the 1984–85 [[Football League Fourth Division]]. The vote went as follows:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:left;"
!width=140| Club
!width=185| Final Position
!width=50| Votes
|-
| [[Northampton Town F.C.|Northampton Town]] || 23rd (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 52
|-
| [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]] || 22nd (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 50
|-
| [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]] || 24th (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 50
|-
| [[Halifax Town A.F.C.|Halifax Town]] || 21st (Fourth Division) ||align=center| 48
|-
| [[Bath City F.C.|Bath City]] || 4th (Alliance Premier League) ||align=center| 8
|}

As a result of this, all four Football League teams were re-elected, and Bath City were denied membership of the Football League.
